neighbours.label: how a problem is framed or approached (jump into a solution, only a hammer, inside the box, how the debate was framed); the same work without the framing word stays quiet
fire: Too many teams jump into implementation before they understand the problem.
If the only tool you have is a hammer, every problem starts to look like a nail.
Sometimes thinking inside the box produces the most practical answer.
Ask yourself afterwards how the whole debate was framed from the start.
Good researchers spend time shaping the research questions before collecting data.
The consultants framed the issue as a cost problem rather than a safety problem.
Don't rush into a fix; first decide which question you are really answering.
The way the agenda was set made some solutions impossible to even discuss.
quiet: Too many teams finish implementation before the end of the month.
If the only car you have is old, every trip starts to take a little longer.
Sometimes working in the office produces the most practical results.
Ask yourself afterwards how long the whole debate actually lasted.
Good researchers spend time cleaning the lab before collecting data.
The consultants sent the report to the board on a Tuesday afternoon.
Don't rush home after work; first check that the doors are locked.
The meeting was held in a small room on the second floor.
